key_prerequisites.name: The Area of an Equilateral Triangle

sections.normalized_html: A circle of radius [MATH: 7 \: \text{cm}] is inscribed into an equilateral triangle, as shown above. What is the area of the triangle?
sections.readable_text:
A circle of radius [MATH: 7 \: \text{cm}] is inscribed into an equilateral triangle, as shown above. What is the area of the triangle?

[IMG: /graphics/51d0ecd38fe66bd2705ade46932b4af0]

sections.normalized_html:
To find the side length of the triangle, we draw line segments from the center to each of the triangle’s vertices. This forms three identical isosceles triangles, each with a central angle of [MATH: 120^\circ,] as shown below.

Now, we take one of these isosceles triangles and draw an altitude from the center to the opposite side. This divides the triangle into two right triangles with angles [MATH: 30^\circ], [MATH: 60^\circ], and [MATH: 90^\circ.]

In each [MATH: 30]-[MATH: 60]-[MATH: 90] triangle:

  • Let the longer leg, which is opposite the [MATH: 60^\circ] angle, be [MATH: x.] Notice that it is half of our equilateral triangle's side length.

  • The shorter leg is the radius [MATH: r = 7 \: \text{cm}] of the circle.

Next, in the [MATH: 30]-[MATH: 60]-[MATH: 90] triangle, the longer leg is [MATH: \sqrt{3}] times the shorter leg:

[MATH: x|= r ⋅ sqrt(3); = 7 ⋅ sqrt(3); = 7sqrt(3)cm]

Therefore, our equilateral triangle's side length is [MATH: s = 2 \cdot 7 \sqrt{3} = 14 \sqrt{3} \: \text{cm},] and the corresponding area of the triangle is [MATH: A|= (sqrt(3))/(4)s^{2}; = (sqrt(3))/(4)(14sqrt(3))^{2}; = (sqrt(3))/(4) ⋅ 588; = 147sqrt(3)cm^{2}.]

  • The longer leg [MATH: x,] which is opposite the [MATH: 60^\circ] angle, is half of our equilateral triangle's side length: [MATH: x = \dfrac{ML}{2} = \dfrac{72}{2} = 36]

  • The shorter leg is the radius [MATH: r] of the circle.

Finally, in the [MATH: 30]-[MATH: 60]-[MATH: 90] triangle, the longer leg is [MATH: \sqrt{3}] times the shorter leg:

[MATH: x|= r ⋅ sqrt(3); 36|= r ⋅ sqrt(3); r|= (36)/(sqrt(3)); = (36)/(sqrt(3)) ⋅ (sqrt(3))/(sqrt(3)); = (36sqrt(3))/(3); = 12sqrt(3)]

Therefore, the radius of the circle is [MATH: 12\sqrt{3} \: \text{ft}.]
